correctness.rationale: The three explicit moment summands in the primary Richardson paper give 34 distinct sums and the displayed eight primitive facet rays. Rational vertex enumeration yields 16 simple unimodular maximal cones, four opposite-ray pairs, and Picard rank 8−4=4. Primitive relations have degrees 0,0,2,2, so −K is nef, big and not ample. For character m=(1,1,1,1), 1−<m,r_i>=(0,0,0,0,2,2,2,2), yielding −K=2L; opposite primitive rays prevent divisibility by >2. The anticanonical polytope has 12 lattice vertices, eight simple vertices and four nonsimple 5-ray vertices; its fan merges 16 cones into eight isolated ones and four square-adjacent pairs. These yield exactly two disjoint exceptional P1×P1 surfaces V(r1,r4), V(r3,r6), mapping along one ruling to disjoint P1 curves, with transverse unimodular conifold square cone uv−wz=0. No ray is contracted, so contraction is small and crepant, target toric Gorenstein Fano. Ehrhart L-polytope counts [1,14,69,216,525] give L^4=20, (−K)^4=320. Independent exact matrix determinants and active-inequality counts confirm 16/12 vertices and four 5-ray nonsimplicial charts; finite checker supports, rather than replaces, toric fan/orbit arguments.

originality.rationale: The 2026-10-26 theorem already identifies this very fourfold as weak Fano, non-Fano, with anticanonical degree 320 and four zero-degree invariant curves. Gorsky–Kim–Sherman-Bennett Example 5.2 already specifies its toric polytope. However neither inspected source determines the entire anticanonical contraction geometry, the two disjoint exceptional ruled surfaces, their images and local conifold singularities, or the primitive half-anticanonical degree L^4=20. Those remain an original classification by best accessible evidence.
